---
title: "1. N.I.C.E. Design Process"
description: "The N.I.C.E. iterative design process used in TAS."
---

> **These notes are unfinished intentionally.** Students will add examples, diagrams, and evidence from our own projects.

## N — Needs & Necessities

Identify what the design must do before deciding what it should look like.

Consider:

- the user or audience
- required functions
- restrictions and constraints
- safety
- available time, tools, materials, and budget
- necessities versus useful extras

## I — Investigate & Inquire

Ask questions before jumping to a solution.

- What already exists?
- What works well?
- What fails?
- What can we measure, test, compare, or research?
- What do we still need to know?

## C — Create & Communicate

Make something that can be tested.

This may be a sketch, prototype, CAD model, circuit, animation, web page, physical object, or explanation.

Communicate the decisions clearly enough that another person can understand what you tried and why.

## E — Evaluate

Compare the result against the needs and evidence.

- What worked?
- What did not?
- What changed?
- What should be improved?
- Did the original requirements still make sense?

Then repeat the cycle with better information.
